URL: https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/7/28/trump-says-good-chance-of-progress-in-iran-talks-what-we-know
(WebFetch extract — Al Jazeera's own reporting language)

Trump: US in "very friendly negotiations" with Iran after pausing strikes; said there was "a good chance" of progress in talks aimed at ending months of fighting; reiterated warning that "military action could resume if negotiations fail."

Iran FM spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei: Iran was "not negotiating with the United States" but "intermediaries may convey messages from the American side to us regarding ongoing developments in the region."

Iran's Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf: "The administration of the strait will never return to the way that it was before the war."

Hormuz talks: renewed indirect talks continued with the Strait of Hormuz at the centre. June 17 MOU committed Iran to facilitating commercial shipping freely for an initial 60-day period; Tehran says this means it controls the route and hinted transit charges could follow the 60-day term.
Mediators: Oman (leading), Qatar, Pakistan, Egypt, plus Trump envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner.
Figures: ~one-fifth of world oil and LNG supplies pass through the strait in peacetime; ~130 ships passed daily before the Feb 28 closures.
